# Modeling views

These are proposed practical distinctions, not an exhaustive philosophical classification. A modeling view is not automatically a domain primitive such as a need or system.

| View | Question | Illustration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ontology | What do the concepts mean, and which relationships are meaningful? | A review has participants, inputs and intended outputs. |
| Taxonomy | What kind of thing is this, and by which classification rule? | The review activity is a process; the page explaining it is a process description; Monday's review is a particular execution. |
| Mereology | What is part of what, in which sense? | Source review is part of a wider learning-to-writing process. |
| Execution and behavior | How do things interact and produce outcomes? | Review produces candidates; selection determines which proceed. |
| Occurrences and history | Which particular things happened, when, in which context? | A particular review considered particular sources and selected a topic. |
| Assessment | What was achieved against which expectations and conditions? | Source coverage was incomplete for the examined run. |

The owner's “mirology” was interpreted by the assistant as **mereology**. [The source account](../../../source-locators.md#source-75f935a4b2184a88) supports the parts-and-wholes meaning. Composition alone does not explain behavior.

“Is a kind of,” “is an instance of,” “is part of,” “depends on,” and “contributes to” are distinct relations. A process is not a kind of system merely because it contributes to or is part of one. A requirement describes expectations and is not necessarily an operating component.

The owner's knowledge-graph/context-graph question captures the need for situated history. We need not commit to that terminology, separate graph types or a graph database to represent occurrences and provenance. [PROV-O](../../../source-locators.md#source-4ba3b6a5c02fa703) supplies comparison concepts, not an adopted schema.

See [ontology](../../../source-locators.md#source-5a5f0f2c1d016afb), [classification](../taxonomy/classification-rules.md), [composition](../mereology/composition-and-boundaries.md), and [records](../information-model/records-and-provenance.md). EOM-01 and EOM-10 remain open in [the ledger](../../../source-locators.md#source-c43947fdcdae322a).
